subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: What should OpenClaw's durable idempotency boundary be for sub-agent actions when the request may have committed but the acknowledgement was lost?
rationale: The remaining fix is not a mechanical bug patch: maintainers need to choose whether logical-action identity belongs in core sub-agent/session state, gateway method idempotency, plugin/tool APIs, or documented external-service contracts.

options.title: Define Core Logical-Action Idempotency
options.body: Add a durable action identity and claim/replay state for OpenClaw-owned sub-agent side effects while documenting that third-party APIs still need their own idempotency support.

options.title: Limit Scope To Delivery Paths
options.body: Keep core guarantees limited to message-tool, announce, and delivery-queue side effects, and document external API idempotency as plugin/skill responsibility.

options.title: Track As Broader Runtime Recovery
options.body: Fold this issue into a larger session recovery and timeout state-machine design before adding any new idempotency surface.

recommendation.title: Define Core Logical-Action Idempotency
recommendation.body: Add a durable action identity and claim/replay state for OpenClaw-owned sub-agent side effects while documenting that third-party APIs still need their own idempotency support.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently worked on outbound recovery replay hardening, which is closest to the remaining side-effect boundary after the message-tool mitigation.
